blocking_finding.detail: The exact M1183 E8 release and its author receipt do not define a complete exact local-to-remote transfer set. Local dependency references are not proof that the remote repository contains the hammered bytes. The omitted closure includes the source, base source contract, source test required by M1181 runtime verification, M1175 review, the complete M1181 review/manifest/outer directory, canonical-40 manifest and both seals, profiler, evaluator checked even in E8, both cohort authority files, and all 40 NPZ payloads.
blocking_finding.consequence: The published command may fail before consuming the one-shot marker, or may execute against unverified/stale remote dependencies. No exact transfer set or launch command is authorized by this hammer.

minimum_non_overwriting_repair: Author a non-overwriting successor sealed handoff-release envelope that binds the exact M1183 launch contract; do not edit M1183 or add keys that its exact runtime schema would reject.

Put a strict remote_transfer_closure in that envelope with remote repo, exact local path, exact remote path, size and SHA256 for every directly checked runtime dependency, both cohort authorities and exactly 40 canonical NPZ rows.
Include the source test because verify_hammer_directory compares it to M1181, and include the evaluator because validate_launch checks its SHA even in E8 mode.

Bind a remote preflight that checks Python 3.10.20, all transfer bytes, checkpoint/config identity, absent output/attempt namespaces, free canonical flock, idle GPU, and absence of legacy M511 including SIGSTOP without consuming the attempt marker.
Require a fresh different-author hammer of the successor release before the single zero-retry launch, then a fresh result hammer after the double-sealed output appears.
